text:
eli: Heads-up: we're starting Cloud KMS integration work for Private deployments (VPC + on‑prem package). Question: SA pattern — bind KMS perms to the node/service account vs create a dedicated kms-encryptor SA and use Workload Identity/impersonation. Need least-priv, rotation plan, and clear audit logging.

rachel: I prefer a dedicated SA + Workload Identity for GKE. Scope the binding down to the cryptoKey resource and give roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter only. If you need to impersonate from app SA, grant roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the kms SA.

jamie: Note for on‑prem (air‑gapped or VM installs) WI isn't available. For those, avoid long‑lived JSON keys. Use short‑lived tokens where possible or a small sidecar that holds ephemeral creds and talks to KMS. We should document both flows.

eli: Good point. For rotation: do we create new cryptoKeyVersions and rewrap envelopes, or rotate the key resource entirely? Also what's our key ring strategy (per-env vs central)? Any compliance caveats?

rachel: Operationally: rotate by creating a new cryptoKeyVersion and rewrap existing envelope keys to the new version (re‑encrypt the DEKs). Keep previous versions until rewrap completes. For layout: per‑project/per‑env key rings (prod/stage/dev) and regional keys close to workloads for latency/compliance.

jamie: Don't forget audit logs: Cloud KMS Data Access logs are off by default and are required to track decrypt/encrypt operations. Enable Admin Activity + Data Access and export to our logging sink (BigQuery/Cloud Logging). It's noisy and costs money but necessary for incident investigations.

kms-bot: Notice: IAM policy binding added by rachel — serviceAccount:kms-encryptor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -> roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on projects/redwood-prod/locations/us/keyRings/private-kr/cryptoKeys/rw-envelope-key

eli: Perfect. Action items: rachel to author exact IAM + Terraform snippet; jamie to add audit log sink and cost estimate; I'll draft the rotation/runbook including rewrap steps and rollback. Anything else?

rachel: I'll post the terraform example and caveats. Example snippet (quick):

```
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "encryptor" {
  crypto_key_id = "projects/redwood-prod/locations/us/keyRings/private-kr/cryptoKeys/rw-envelope-key"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  member        = "serviceAccount:kms-encryptor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}
```

Also: avoid using roles/cloudkms.admin except for a small ops group. If we need cross-project access, prefer explicit bindings rather than broad project roles.

jamie: :thumbsup: Runtime note — set envelope key cache TTL (e.g., 5m) and a short offline fallback policy (e.g., fallback to in‑memory ephemeral DEK for 30s with alert). Add monitoring for KMS RPC error rates and a pager for sustained failures.

eli: Thanks, everyone. I'll collect the docs and link in this thread when ready.
